title: GeoSpectra Lab — A Falsification-First Validation Harness for Discretized Spectral Operators on Compact Product Manifolds (v0.1.24)
description: GeoSpectra Lab is a falsification-first validation harness for discretized spectral operators on finite-lattice compact product toy manifolds. The Gate 4B v0.1.24 corrected campaign (216 cases, S³×S¹) plus negative-controls campaign v0.1.22 (54 cases) plus wilson-scrambled extension (18 cases) plus spectral-circle extension (18 cases) — 306 cases total — produced the FINAL verdict DISCRETIZATION_SENSITIVE / GEOMETRY_AGNOSTIC: the harness distinguishes lattice product structure from random / scrambled / broken baselines (specificity to Level 3 — FFT vs lattice discretization), but does NOT distinguish Wilson-term internal details (Level 5). Aggregate true-IPR contrast (W=20 vs W=0) preserved at 7.07× after S³ Dirac operator correction (versus 7.15× before correction, change less than 1.1%). This is a methodology paper, NOT a physical compactification proof. All validation on finite-lattice toy operators (N ≤ 896). Eight scientific non-claims explicitly stated: no continuum compactification, no S⁶ or S³×S⁶ validation, no Standard Model derivation, no physical chirality, no Witten/Lichnerowicz bypass, no physical extra dimensions, no hierarchy solution, no observable predictions.
notes: This work validates a falsification-first workflow for discretized toy operators on finite lattices. It does NOT prove continuum compactification, Standard Model derivation, physical chirality, or S⁶/Calabi-Yau validation. Inspired by but independent from Tom Lawrence's covariant compactification framework; per Tom Lawrence's own assessment (CAMP, 2026-05-26), S³×S¹ is closer to original Kaluza-Klein than to covariant compactification, which requires at least two extra dimensions.
